title: Rename Logwolf to Logray
description:
Switch to the name "Logray" for the log analyzer. Rays are biological
cousins of sharks and more people like the name "Logray" in a completely
unscientific survey here. Apologies for any inconvenience this might
cause.

notes.body: Unless anyone has a strong preference for "Logwolf" I plan on merging this next Tuesday, the 5th.

I haven't really been paying too much attention to Logwolf/Logray, so I don't really know much about it other than what's in the docbook/logwolf-quick-start.adoc file, but perhaps there'll be some information presented at Sharkfest about it?

Should there be a README.logray file too, one that is more suited for users, as the quick-start guide seems much more geared toward developers?  Also, I didn't notice anything mentioned in the last 3.7.1 release notes about it ... should there be?

Loris and I are scheduled to talk about it in the Day 2 keynote on the 13th. Along with a README we need a man page and User's Guide, but I don't know when those might appear. The current plan is to have a separate release cycle and packages for Logray, so it will likely have its own release notes.

Yes, but his name is pronounced [loʊgreɪ](https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Logray/Legends), however *that* is pronounced.  Again, I know next to nothing about logray, but if a fish-related name having to do with logs is desired, then interestingly  the [Mangrove Rivulus](https://www.nationalgeographic.com/animals/article/fish-lives-inside-logs-breathing-air-for-months) is a species of fish that lives in logs for up to months at a time, so potentially _rivulus_ could be a name to use?  Although I suspect rivulus is less likely to be recognized as something to do with processing log files than a name like Logfoo would be ... unless it's just me lacking much knowledge in fish species.

And then there's the [Panaque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panaque), the fish that feeds extensively on wood (logs?)  Logray is just fine though; I merely got to thinking about fish+logs and these things popped up in my Google searches.  I blame Chuck for starting this. :smile:

Being firmly in the Star Trek camp, I don't know enough whether to embrace, or be embarrassed by Mr. Ray.  
There are plenty of Google hits [Ethereal-users: Re: [Ethereal-users] Why the name change?](https://www.wireshark.org/lists/ethereal-users/200606/msg00131.html) for the name change to Wireshark but none with an explanation for its etymology. I can only assume that `LANshark` was too easily confused with [landshark](https://www.nbc.com/saturday-night-live/video/landshark/2832305). Has the `Wireshark` name origin ever been revealed or is that lost like secrets of building the pyramids and where Maroon 5 got its name? It's well known that the three (and four) letter agencies have a CRAY (or a least a beefy Raspberry Pi) deep in their bowels for coming up with codenames for projects. "a completely unscientific survey" sounds a lot like "our team of experts back at the lab" so SGTM. :-)

He is an Ewok, embrace him. But it is a good point to make, I would be very weary to name something after a character a big studio like Disney has rights on. Not saying that they apply here (not by a longshot in any case), but the term seems to be wildly used on the Internet. 

If we are staying in the area of fishing, the remora would be a fish - sometimes called suckerfish - which has a deeply symbiotic relationship with sharks and benefits greatly from them. Would better classify the relationship between Wireshark and Logshark. Just don't look up their dietary needs ;-) 

But should the name symbolize anything? Ethereal did not - outside a very small group of people - so why should this be a case here? If it shouldn't represent anything, I would rather have change the name to something completely different, like "Sherlog", for instance. As a word-play it symbolizes exactly what the program is supposed to do, and as a name it carries association to an investigative somebody. There is however a security company that utilizes that name, so that could be an issue.

> Has the `Wireshark` name origin ever been revealed or is that lost like secrets of building the pyramids and where Maroon 5 got its name?

When it became apparent that we weren't going to be able to continue under the name "Ethereal", we collected a list of candidate names and "Wireshark" was the one that stood out. In particular it passed the "Karen test" — I showed the list of names to my wife Karen and she picked Wireshark.

Although I'd be fine with Logwolf, I do prefer Logray and it passes the Karen Test this time around. As for the Star Wars character, there's a pretty clear distinction between a cartilaginous-fish-species-themed log analyzer and a furry alien's given name, just as there's a clear distinction between McDonald Supply (which sells toilets) and McDonald's (which sells fast food).

commits_data.message:
Rename Logwolf to Logray

Switch to the name "Logray" for the log analyzer. Rays are biological
cousins of sharks and more people like the name "Logray" in a completely
unscientific survey here. Apologies for any inconvenience this might
cause.
